founder.title: Why Kaneo exists
founder.intro: I'm Andrej, and I created Kaneo because I was tired of project management tools that got in the way more than they helped. After years of using bloated, overcomplicated platforms that distracted from actual work, I knew there had to be a better way.
founder.problem: The problem wasn't that these tools lacked features - it was that they had too many. Every notification, every unnecessary button, every complex workflow was pulling my team away from what mattered: building great products.
founder.principle: I believe the best tools are invisible. They should amplify your team's natural workflow, not force you to adapt to theirs. Kaneo is built on the principle that less is more - every feature exists because it solves a real problem, not because it looks impressive in a demo.

product.title: Before you get started
product.description: The practical details about hosting, planning, and connecting your team.
product.overview: Kaneo is an open-source, MIT-licensed project management platform with boards, backlog, Gantt and calendar views, custom fields, time tracking, and GitHub integration. Self-host it on your own infrastructure or use Kaneo Cloud.

hosting.question: Is Kaneo free to self-host?
hosting.answer: Yes. Kaneo is MIT licensed and free to self-host, with single sign-on included. Run the application alongside PostgreSQL using Docker Compose, or deploy with the official Helm chart. You manage infrastructure, updates, and backups.

planning.question: Does Kaneo have Gantt charts?
planning.answer: Yes. Kaneo includes Gantt and calendar views alongside boards, lists, and backlog planning. Use task start dates and due dates to plan work on a timeline. Budgeting, baseline comparisons, and sprint burndown reports are outside its current scope.

sso.question: Is single sign-on included?
sso.answer: Yes. The free self-hosted build supports Google, GitHub, Discord, and custom OAuth/OIDC providers. Configure your provider on your instance without purchasing a separate Kaneo edition.

agents.question: Can AI clients work with Kaneo?
agents.answer: Yes. Kaneo provides an MCP server through the @kaneo/mcp package and an HTTP endpoint. Compatible AI clients can read and update tasks using an API key tied to a user, subject to workspace permissions.

selfHostingGuide.summary: What self-hosting involves, with links to the maintained Docker Compose configuration and installation steps.
selfHostingGuide.answer: To self-host Kaneo, run the application and PostgreSQL with Docker Compose, configure your public URL and secrets, and put a TLS reverse proxy in front. The installation guide specifies at least 2 GB of RAM and 10 GB of disk space. Plan for ongoing updates, database backups, and storage for uploaded files.
selfHostingGuide.requirements: The documented minimum is 2 GB of RAM and 10 GB of disk space, with Docker 20.10 or newer and Docker Compose V2. Allow more capacity for your workload, database growth, and uploaded files.
selfHostingGuide.compose: Use the maintained compose.yml in the Docker Compose guide. It defines PostgreSQL, a persistent database volume, the Kaneo application, and health checks. Configure the environment file before starting the services; for production, pin an image version so updates are deliberate.
selfHostingGuide.backups: Back up both PostgreSQL and any object storage used for uploads. Choose a schedule based on how much work your team can afford to lose, store copies off the application server, and test restoring them before you need them.
selfHostingGuide.worth: Self-hosting makes sense when you need control over infrastructure and data, and someone can own maintenance. Include server capacity, storage, backups, and that maintenance time when comparing costs with a managed service.
selfHostingGuide.minimum: The installation guide specifies Docker 20.10 or newer, Docker Compose V2, at least 2 GB of RAM, and 10 GB of disk space. The Compose setup includes PostgreSQL. Redis is optional for a single API instance.
